About Teramind
Teramind is a global leader in workforce intelligence, insider risk management, and data loss prevention. Used by thousands of companies across 60+ countries, our platform gives organizations the visibility to protect their people, their data, and their operations. We sit at the intersection of three converging markets - Insider Risk, DLP, and Workforce Analytics - and we are one of the few players that spans all three on a unified behavioral data layer.
The Teramind Endpoint Agent is one of the key differentiators of our platform. It runs on hundreds of thousands of endpoints across Windows, macOS, and Linux, capturing the behavioral signal that powers our detection, DLP enforcement, analytics, and AI. The depth and quality of what the Agent sees is a primary reason customers choose Teramind over the alternatives - and the product leader who owns it plays a pivotal role in the company's success.

We are hiring a Senior Product Manager to own the Teramind Endpoint Agent, and the AI Usage Control capabilities built on top of it, end to end.

You will be the single accountable product leader for the roadmap, priorities, and outcomes of the Agent organization - approximately half of Teramind engineering, working across operating systems, low-level platform components, and the server-side telemetry pipeline. This is a pivotal role.

The Agent is one of the strongest competitive moats Teramind has, and the next chapter of the product strategy depends on what we build into it. You are coming in to bring product rigor, customer insight, prioritization discipline, and technical judgment to a team that is capable of shipping world-class endpoint technology.

AI Usage Control is one of the most important things you will build here. Companies have spent twenty years governing what employees do with sensitive data, and they now have a second workforce: AI agents reading files, calling tools, and executing commands on the same machines, with none of the accountability.

Nobody has worked out what supervising them looks like, and much of it never touches the network, so the endpoint is the only place you can see it. You will own that end to end. You will sit alongside other product managers, reporting to the VP of Product. Together, you own Teramind's product surface area.
What You Will Own
The Agent roadmap across all platforms. Windows, macOS, Linux, and the platforms after them. You decide what ships, in what order, and why, balancing customer demand, platform modernization, performance, and security hardening on one prioritized backlog.
The endpoint layer of AI Usage Control . Detecting AI that never touches the network - native desktop clients, IDE-embedded assistants, terminal-based coding agents, AI-native Teramind | Senior Product Manager, AI and Endpoint browsers, and local models running offline - and capturing the prompts, pastes, uploads, and agent-executed commands that browser and network DLP cannot see.
Translating business vision into engineering reality . You turn signals from executives, sales, customers, competitors and the engineering org into a coherent technical roadmap. You are the interpreter between “we need to detect AI exfiltration” and “here is how we instrument the endpoint to see it.”
Building for the enterprise: bulletproof and undetectable . Enterprise customers expect the Agent to be invisible to end users, resilient against tampering, and reliable in conditions that break weaker products. You own the roadmap that keeps it that way.
Performance, footprint, and reliability. Every CPU cycle, megabyte and battery percent we consume is felt by the end user and argued about by the customer's IT team. You set and defend the performance bar.
Define, measure, and meet product KPIs. Adoption, rollout velocity, deployment success rate, crash rates, detection coverage, time-to-patch on OS changes. You set the numbers and hold the team and the company to them.
Industry and ecosystem relationships. Microsoft, Apple, the Linux ecosystem, MDM vendors, and the major AV and EDR vendors. You represent Teramind in technical conversations where the agent's architecture is the subject.

5+ years of product management experience , with at least 3 owning a technical platform, SDK, agent, or systems-level product. This is a senior IC seat: influence without headcount.
Technical depth is non-negotiable . You do not need to write C++, but you should reason about Windows architecture, macOS system extensions, and the trade-offs between Endpoint Security and Network Extension frameworks. You can push back credibly in a design review.
You understand how AI actually runs on a computer . A hosted model in a browser tab, a native desktop client, an IDE-embedded assistant, a CLI coding agent, and a local model under Ollama are five different detection problems, and several are invisible to anything watching the network. You know why, and you know what an audit trail for an autonomous agent has to capture.
Endpoint or systems background. You have shipped endpoint security (EDR, EPP, XDR), monitoring or management agents, OS-level tools, or systems software. CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Defender, Tanium and similar are directly relevant. Pure SaaS and application PMs without systems exposure will struggle here.
You think in outcomes, not features. Success is “95% of customers roll out a new agent version within 30 days,” not “shipped version 27.0.”
You are comfortable with security trade-offs. Visibility versus privacy, tamper protection versus usability, cloud processing versus on-device intelligence. You can hold the attacker's perspective and the IT buyer's perspective in the same conversation.
You work with AI, not just about it. You use AI in your own practice, prototyping to pressure-test concepts before spending engineering cycles, and evaluating model behavior rather than trusting vendor claims.
You bring rigor, and you write. PRDs, decision memos, prioritization frameworks, release cadence, credible engineering-facing specs. In a distributed team, writing is how product management scales.

Engineering background earlier in your career: systems, kernel, driver, or low-level platform work
Windows Filter Drivers, Minifilters or WFP; macOS Endpoint Security or Network Extensions; Linux eBPF, kernel modules or userspace agents
MDM ecosystems (Jamf, Intune, Workspace ONE, Kandji)
Insider risk, DLP, or behavioral analytics
Local model runtimes and on-device inference (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp)
Agentic AI: tool calling, MCP, and autonomous coding or workflow agents
AI governance, AI security, or shadow AI discovery products
EDR and AV co-existence and exclusion lists at scale
Why This Role
Endpoint agents are having a moment. The convergence of insider risk, DLP, AI, and hybrid work is making the endpoint the most strategically important surface in enterprise security and workforce intelligence. Teramind's Agent is one of the deepest data-collection engines in the market - we see things the rest of the category does not - and it is one of the strongest competitive moats we have.

Do you know what product management is really about? If you do, then you know it isn't roadmaps, tickets or beautifully groomed backlogs. It's finding a real, expensive, unglamorous problem that people live with every day - and shipping something that makes it go away. That is product.
At Shape Construction, we are building software that transforms how construction projects are delivered. It's born out of real project experience and designed to bring clarity, structure and performance to complex environments.
The problem we are solving is one of the oldest in the industry: what actually happens on a construction site never makes it, intact, to the people who need it. Supervisors, field engineers and site managers see reality first: work blocked, plans deviated from, instructions given verbally, conditions nobody planned for.

That knowledge lives in heads, notebooks, camera rolls and group chats. Meanwhile the people responsible for the commercial health of the project are working weeks behind, from whatever fragments they can piece together. By the time anyone needs to prove what happened, the evidence has gone cold.
We are building the platform that closes that gap. Tools the site genuinely wants to use, capturing what happens as it happens, and then turning that raw signal into structured, trustworthy records that let commercial and project leadership make decisions, hold their ground and protect margin they would otherwise have written off.
This is your opportunity to own a core part of that. You won't be handed a roadmap to administer, you'll shape it, defend it, and be measured on whether customers are genuinely better off. If you like being close to messy real-world problems, have strong opinions about what to build and the discipline to kill your own ideas when the evidence says so, keep reading.

As a Product Manager you'll own a core area of the Shape platform end to end, from the customer problem through to the outcome it produces on a live project.
You'll be accountable for a measurable business outcome for our customers, not for a feature list. Our platform spans two very different worlds, and both matter. On one side, the site: supervisors, field engineers and site managers working in conditions where an app has about five seconds to prove it's worth opening.

On the other, the office: project directors, commercial directors and quantity surveyors who need to trust what they're looking at enough to make a call on it. Value only appears when those two sides connect, and that connection is what we build.
Depending on where you're strongest and what the business needs, you might own the field side, the commercial side, or the seam between them. In every case the standard is the same: real adoption by people who have no obligation to use us, and a concrete outcome for the project as a result.
You'll also be at the front of how AI shows up in our products. A meaningful part of our ambition depends on AI doing genuinely hard things well in a domain with very little tolerance for confident nonsense, the stakes for our users are commercial and often contractual. You'll be the person who decides where AI earns its place, and where it doesn't.
Team
You'll be part of our Product team, working shoulder to shoulder with engineering, design, and our consultancy delivery teams, who are on live projects every day and are the sharpest feedback loop any product team could ask for. You'll also work closely with growth and customer success to make sure what we build reaches the people who need it.

Own the outcome: You will own a product area end to end, the problem, the strategy, the roadmap and the results. You'll define what success looks like in customer and commercial terms, and you'll be honest about whether we hit it.
Get close to the problem, on both sides: You'll spend real time on live projects, in the site cabin and in the commercial meeting, with our consultancy teams, and in the data. You'll build a deeper understanding of how a construction project actually runs, and of the commercial machinery behind it, than most people in our industry have, and use it to make sharp calls about what to build and what to refuse.

In just five years, Stora has become the platform behind more than 30% of UK self storage locations, and we're scaling globally from here. Operators have processed over £150m in automated payments through us, and see an average of 32% business growth after they switch.
We're doing this in a market that's wide open. Europe has over 10,000 self storage sites and is growing fast, yet it sits years behind the US on maturity and is still barely touched by good software. The UK is our stronghold. The rest of Europe is where we're heading next.
Stora is the operating system for modern self storage: online bookings, payments, facility management, reporting, and automation in one platform. We started as operators ourselves, and that's still how we think. If you want to own a product operators depend on every day, in a company genuinely rethinking how it builds, this is it.
Why this role matters
We have a strong product team, great engineers, and a growing product. The bottleneck isn't ideas or execution capacity. It's people who can hold the full picture at once.
What the business needs, what the customer actually experiences, what's technically feasible, what to cut when time is short, and knowing when to slow down. Making good calls across all of it. That's the job.
We've shortened the loop between insight and shipped product by stripping out the layers that slow good judgement down. The quality bar didn't move. This role exists to keep doing that. It carries real ownership from day one, and the scope grows as Stora does.
The surface you'd own
This is the product operators live in every day, and the storefront their own customers book through. You're designing for two users at once: the operator running the business, and the end customer renting the unit. Getting that B2B2C experience right is a genuine craft problem. It's a broad, central surface, and it's heavy on UX.

Core workflows: customers, units, tenancies, access
Roles, permissions, account structure
Operational reporting: occupancy, utilisation, activity
The internal data layer: event tracking, core models, metric definitions
The growth surface: storefront, checkout, the lead → booking funnel
If an operator uses it daily, or relies on it to understand their business, it sits with this team.
How we actually work
We've changed how product gets built at Stora. This is how we operate now.
Designers work directly in the codebase. Engineers and product people work closely together from the start. We use AI genuinely: to explore, prototype and move faster. The work gets closer to reality, sooner.
If you're at a company that talks about moving faster but runs the same process it did three years ago, this will feel different. We're not done evolving how we work, and this person will have real scope to shape that.

s.t:
Transforme sua carreira com o iFood ! Somos uma empresa brasileira de tecnologia referência na América Latina. Por meio de soluções inovadoras, conectamos milhares de restaurantes a milhões de consumidores diariamente com uma média de 100 milhões de pedidos mensais. Além do delivery de comida, também somos Mercado, Farmácia e Pet.

Temos também o iFood Pago, nossa Fintech, que engloba o iFood Benefícios, o vale alimentação e refeição do iFood e o próprio iFood Pago, o banco do restaurante. Junte-se a nós e faça parte de uma equipe que está sempre à frente com tecnologia de ponta e inovação constante.

Who we are
Help Scout started in 2011 with a simple premise: support software should treat customers like people, not tickets. 3+ billion conversations later, more than 10,000 companies use Help Scout to grow relationships with customers of all types, from clients to patients and beyond.
Now we’re in a new chapter: not only building AI that gives teams more space to focus on the customer experience, but also reimagining how we operate in an AI-native world. That means shipping and learning faster, without compromising on craft. Great work here carries a strong opinion and sweats the details, regardless of the tools we use to drive it.
We’ve been a fully remote team since day one, with 120+ teammates now all over the world. It’s a culture where you’ll be trusted to take ownership, stay curious, and raise the quality of work around you. It comes with clear expectations and a team that will push you to do some of the best work of your career.
If that kind of challenge gives you energy, we’d love to meet you.

Help Scout has earned something most software companies never get: genuine trust. More than 10,000 businesses use us, and a remarkable share of them arrived because someone they respect recommended Help Scout. Our brand reputation is the foundation for something bigger.
The support industry is changing shape, and a key part of Help Scout's future growth will come from outcome-based products: resolutions handled, drafts sent, actions taken on behalf of a customer. Making sure customers discover those, see value in them, and build habits around them is a key part of the impact of your role.
Growth at Help Scout spans the entire customer journey: turning sign-ups into trials, how quickly a trial gets set up to see value, and how customers who love one part of Help Scout find their way into the products they aren't using yet.

You'll own the vision, roadmap, and execution for the Growth workstream in partnership with design and engineering.
That starts with sharpening the core funnel: signup, onboarding, trial-to-paid conversion, and the activation moments that turn a trial into a team that can't imagine working without Help Scout.
Second, help strengthen the expansion motion for our AI product lines. Every surface of the product should help customers discover and adopt what's next for them, and you'll own how that works.
Third, scale growth capability across the org. You'll set up the frameworks, metrics, and experiment practices that let other teams run their own growth work, so growth thinking is embedded everywhere rather than concentrated in one workstream.
You'll report to Scott Rocher, our Chief Product Officer.
Note: This role is open to US-based applicants only.
This role is currently open to consideration at 2 levels. The compensation range reflects the range across both levels.

Own the full growth roadmap: signup, onboarding, activation, trial-to-paid conversion, and in-product expansion into our AI product lines
Build and run a high-tempo experimentation practice, with the discipline to know when a result is signal and when it's noise
Design how customers discover and adopt new products from inside Help Scout, partnering closely with the PMs who own each product line
Go after big opportunities, not just optimizations. Some of the highest-impact growth work will be things we've never done before
Build the growth model, experiment standards, and playbooks that let teams across the company ship growth work with confidence, without routing every call through you
Bring strategic input to pricing and packaging decisions alongside product, marketing, and finance
Spend real time with customers and in the data, translating what you learn into insight the whole company can act on
Work with marketing, sales, and CS so the growth motion is coherent across the full customer lifecycle

You've spent 5+ years in Product with direct experience leading growth in B2B SaaS with a free trial or freemium motion, and you know how to get customers to the moment where the product's value is undeniable
You love data, and you're hands-on with it. You define the metrics, design the experiments, and you're honest about what the numbers do and don't say
You think in outcomes, not features. "Activated teams" and "expansion revenue" are more interesting to you than "new onboarding flow launched"
You build systems, not just wins. The frameworks and playbooks you leave behind make everyone around you faster
You're genuinely fluent with AI tools and treat them as part of your craft — for research synthesis, strategy testing, rapid prototyping, and customer signal analysis. You have a point of view on where these tools are heading and how they're changing the shape of PM work
You understand that when execution is cheap, judgment is the bottleneck. Your highest-leverage hours are spent on strategy and prioritization — defining what's next and what's not — not on driving the build
You're an excellent writer. Help Scout runs on writing, and you make your thinking visible in one-pagers, briefs, and narratives that move decisions forward
You lead through influence and trust. This is an individual contributor role, and the best growth work happens when engineers, designers, and marketers want to run with you
You've worked in B2B SaaS and understand the difference between building for support teams vs. building for end consumers
Company values
Happy to Help
Help is in our first name! We show up for each other — not out of obligation, but because we’re invested in the team’s collective success. We share knowledge freely, lead with generosity, and practice empathy with our teammates, customers, and community.
Craft over Convention
Our success relies on the quality and craft of the work we put into the world. The status quo simply won’t work. So we insist on narrow focus, sweating every detail, and relentless pursuit of customer delight.
Progress not Perfection
Achieving our true potential — collectively and individually — requires constant progress and forward momentum. By creating a culture of curiosity and openness, we aim to create a safe space for mistakes, the ability to identify them quickly, and use them to get better.
Own the Outcome
Own the outcome means taking full responsibility for the results of your work, decisions, and contributions. It reflects a mindset of accountability, proactiveness, and follow-through. If you “own the outcome,” you don’t just complete tasks, you ensure your work leads to meaningful results, and take initiative to solve problems rather than passing them along.
Read more about how we define, share, and live these values here .

Ajaia is an AI implementation consultancy and product studio. We help organizations move from AI experimentation to measurable return on investment across four practices: AI Strategy and Advisory, Workforce Training and Enablement, Process Optimization, and Custom AI Development. Our work sits with executives and the people who do the work, and it is judged on whether something changed in production, not on whether a pilot looked good in a deck.

Ajaia is hiring a remote Product Manager to own products in Ajaia's product suite end to end. You will talk to users and customers every week, decide what gets built next and why, and say plainly what does not get built, including when the loudest voice in the room wants it.

You will write specs an engineer can build from without a follow-up meeting, prototype with AI tools when a working demo settles an argument faster than a deck, and stay on the number after launch and act on what it tells you. This is a builder's seat: you will contribute to the code and the design yourself, not only direct them.
You will work with a US-based team and US clients. Most of your users, stakeholders, and engineers sit in New York, so this role is built around daily overlap with US Eastern hours, not asynchronous handoffs.
Compensation: Competitive, benchmarked to senior product roles in your market, plus a performance bonus tied to product outcomes. We will share a specific number for your location early in the process.
How we expect you to work
AI use is a core execution requirement at Ajaia, not optional tooling. You will use AI daily to sort through usage data, draft specs, and build working prototypes yourself, and you are judged on what you keep from that output, not on how much of it you generated. The tools change fast, and staying current on what is worth using is part of the job.
Remote works here when the writing is strong. Decisions, specs, and priority calls get written down where the team can read them, not held in your head until the next call.

Talk to users and customers every week. Not a quarterly survey. Real conversations, real usage, on US time.
Turn messy, sometimes contradictory signal, usage data, support tickets, sales requests, and what people say in interviews, into a ranked call on what gets built next.
Say plainly what does not get built, including a well-funded customer's request, when the evidence does not support it.
Write specs an engineer can build from without a follow-up meeting: the outcome, what is in and out of scope, where a human stays in the loop, and acceptance criteria someone could test.
Prototype the core flow yourself, wireframes, a clickable mock, or a working demo, when that settles the argument faster than a deck would.
Contribute to the code and the design directly: ship a small feature or fix with AI tools, mock the screen yourself, and hand engineers something running instead of something described.
Partner with the design team on what the solution should be and how it holds up for the people using it.
Partner with the delivery team and engineers on how the build runs and the date it ships by.
Present the roadmap and the tradeoffs to the people who fund it, including when a client or a salesperson is unhappy with the call.
Hold a priority decision under real pushback, or change it, and say why either way.
Ship it, then watch the number after launch and act on what it says.

Sharp judgment on what to build next, and clear about what not to build.

Deine Aufgaben
* Du führst das Team-Backlog des M365-Teams: du übersetzt Anforderungen in klar geschnittene, priorisierte Backlog-Items, definierst Akzeptanzkriterien und nimmst die Ergebnisse ab.
* In enger Zusammenarbeit mit dem Product Manager M365 setzt du Roadmap und Prioritäten in umsetzbare Arbeitspakete um und vertrittst das Team in den SAFe-Events (PI Planning, PO-Sync, Review, Refinement).

* Neue Begehren wie Copilot, Power Platform oder weitere M365-Dienste bringst du gemeinsam mit den Governance-, Security- und Datenschutzverantwortlichen nachvollziehbar und dokumentiert zur Freigabe.
* Du arbeitest aktiv am Aufbau des neuen M365-Teams mit und bringst agile Arbeitsweisen, eine ausgeprägte Kundenorientierung und einen starken Ownership-Gedanken ein.
Dein Profil
* Abgeschlossene Ausbildung oder Studium in Informatik, Wirtschaftsinformatik oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung (FA, HF, FH oder Universität).
* Mehrjährige Erfahrung als Product Owner oder in einer vergleichbaren Rolle im Umfeld moderner Arbeitsplatz- und Kollaborationslösungen, idealerweise in einem skalierten agilen Setup (SAFe). Du arbeitest selbstorganisiert, proaktiv und übernimmst Verantwortung über den gesamten Lebenszyklus deiner Produkte.

* Du analysierst und priorisierst Anforderungen strukturiert, führst unterschiedliche Stakeholder zu tragfähigen Lösungen und bleibst verbindlich, auch wenn Interessen kollidieren.
* Kommunikationsstärke, vernetztes Denken sowie eine ausgeprägte Kunden- und Dienstleistungsorientierung runden dein Profil ab.

About Magic Eden and Dicey
Magic Eden reached unicorn status in just 9 months after launch, one of the fastest in history. We built a category-defining NFT marketplace from scratch and proved we know how to move fast. Now we're doing it again. Dicey is our crypto casino and sportsbook platform, targeting the $180B+ iGaming and sports betting markets.
We're a small, fully remote team. We ship fast, we're hands-on with our data, and we're rebuilding how a growth team operates around AI from the ground up.

Most of the iGaming industry competes on acquisition. Almost nobody has figured out personalized retention, knowing who a player is, what they need right now, and what would actually change their behavior this week. That's the problem you'll own.
This role focuses on the full post-signup journey: expanding our player segmentation framework, designing and running targeted offers and campaigns, and owning the P&L lever that comes with it. It's explicitly AI-native. You'll build workflows, agents, and pipelines to run lifecycle campaigns that would have taken a whole team two years ago. Half the job is identifying the right problem. The other half is running the experiments to find the answer.

Own retention and monetization as a growth loop. Set the targets, find the leverage, and drive the numbers for everything that happens after a player signs up
Own the player segmentation framework. Today it's value and risk. You decide how it evolves, what signals feed it, and how the rest of the company uses it
Build the AI-native growth stack. Analysis, agents, and automated pipelines that surface segments, generate offer candidates, and run campaigns with minimal manual work
Design and ship targeted offers for specific segments and moments: reload bonuses, lossback, wager bounties, challenges, win-back sequences. Size them, spec them, ship them, measure them
Spend real time in our data warehouse and on-chain data finding patterns and turn them into campaigns before anyone else does
Expand the signals we have on players: on-chain activity, status-match programs, social account linking, and whatever else you can think of
Run the campaigns. Email, in-app, Telegram, whatever the channel. You're hands-on with it, with AI doing the heavy lifting
Partner with engineering and design to ship the product surfaces that make all of this repeatable

Strong intuition for player psychology and incentive design. Experience in gambling, gaming, fintech, or consumer marketplaces helps. Genuine curiosity about why people behave the way they do is required
Deeply analytical. You can go from a vague question to a clean cohort cut yourself, without waiting on a data scientist
AI-native by default. You already use AI to write queries, build analyses, and automate your own work and you want to push that much further
High output with good judgment. You generate a lot of ideas and know which ones are worth testing first
Bias to do it yourself. You're comfortable sending the email, running the query, and writing the spec, not just briefing others
Comfortable with ambiguity. There's no playbook here, you'll be building it

MBB consultant who wants to move into product and own outcomes, not just advise on them
